name: Customer buys a plant
summary: A customer browses the Fern & Fig plant catalogue, opens a plant they like, adds it to their cart, signs in and pays — finishing on an order-confirmation screen. The journey is honest about the ways a purchase can fail: an empty cart has nothing to check out, a plant can sell out between the cart and payment, and a payment can be declined. If the plant they want is already sold out on the detail page, they can ask to be notified instead of buying.

steps.description: The customer browses the whole plant catalogue as a grid of cards showing each plant's name, photo, price and stock badge.

examples.label: Input: Plant mock record; stored sample, not live service data

steps.label: Plant detail
steps.description: The customer opens one plant to see its photo, price and stock, and can add it to the cart.

examples.label: Input: Plant mock record; stored sample, not live service data

examples.label: Input: Plant mock record; stored sample, not live service data
Output: Order mock record; stored sample, not live service data

steps.label: Sign in
steps.description: Before paying, the customer signs in or creates an account so the order is tied to them, and their cart is kept through sign-in.

Output: Order mock record; stored sample, not live service data

branches.label: Notify me
branches.description: The shop replaces the 'Add to cart' button with a 'Notify me' button so the customer can be emailed when the plant is back.

missing_bindings.name: notification_subscription
missing_bindings.reason: The mock design names a notify action but defines no subscription record or response fields.

branches.label: Empty cart
branches.description: The customer opens an empty cart and sees an empty-cart message with a link back to the catalogue instead of a total and a pay button.

io_contracts.not_applicable: This branch renders the empty-cart view when no pending Order record is selected. The mock store has no Cart or empty-cart JSON wrapper; do not fabricate an Order with missing required fields or claim a checkout response.

branches.label: Payment declined
branches.description: The shop places no order, keeps the cart intact and shows the customer a clear error with a way to try a different payment method.

examples.label: Input: Order mock record; stored sample, not live service data
Input: Payment mock record; stored sample, not live service data
Output: Order mock record; stored sample, not live service data

branches.condition: the plant sold out after it was added to the cart
branches.label: Sold out at checkout
branches.description: The shop blocks payment, creates no order and tells the customer the plant is no longer available.

examples.label: Input: Order mock record; stored sample, not live service data
Input: Plant mock record; illustrative state, not an executed mutation

acceptance_scenarios.given: the catalog has in-stock and out-of-stock plants
acceptance_scenarios.then: each plant shows its price and a stock badge (in stock / low / out of stock)

acceptance_scenarios.when: the customer opens its detail page
acceptance_scenarios.then: they can add it to the cart

acceptance_scenarios.given: a plant has been added to the cart
acceptance_scenarios.then: the cart shows the plant, quantity, unit price and a running total before they pay

acceptance_scenarios.when: the customer opens its detail page
acceptance_scenarios.then: the add-to-cart button is replaced by a 'Notify me' action
an empty-cart message is shown, no total or pay button is offered, and a link back to the catalogue is provided

acceptance_scenarios.given: an unauthenticated customer with items in their cart
acceptance_scenarios.then: they are asked to sign in (or create an account) and their cart is preserved once signed in

acceptance_scenarios.given: a cart with at least one item and a signed-in customer
acceptance_scenarios.when: the customer pays and the payment is approved
acceptance_scenarios.then: an Order is created with status 'paid' and the confirmation screen is shown

acceptance_scenarios.given: a cart with at least one item and a signed-in customer
acceptance_scenarios.when: the customer pays and the payment is declined
acceptance_scenarios.then: no Order is created, the cart is preserved, and a clear payment-declined error offers another payment method

acceptance_scenarios.given: a cart holding a plant that has since dropped to zero stock
acceptance_scenarios.then: payment is blocked, no Order is created, and the customer is told the item is no longer available
the confirmation screen shows the order number and the paid items

provenance.note: Seed / gold reference for the future flow agent.

v2: added a sign-in step (auth) and three honest failure branches — empty-cart, payment-declined, and sold-out-at-checkout — so the gold reference stops teaching a happy-path-only journey. Each new node carries reads/writes backed by the catalog dataset and a Given/When/Then scenario, and links to a new UXP L3 AC. Set realization=mock.

v3: the checkout step now expands_to the new fern-and-fig/checkout-and-pay child flow (C4 drill-down). Its impl_status now rolls up from that child's payment sub-journey rather than from UXP-210d alone — extend-not-duplicate: the checkout detail lives in one place and this journey references it.
Document exact source-reviewed or illustrative inputs/outputs; preserve existing AC and lifecycle status. Generated index refresh follows the complete migration.
